newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin able to rule day after operation-doctor.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin able to rule day after operation-doctor.

text.p: Boris Yeltsin should be back ruling Russia and controlling the nuclear "red button" a day after major heart surgery, the chief Kremlin doctor said on Thursday.

Yeltsin, 65, who will have a bypass operation to relieve clogged arteries in six to 10 weeks, has decreed that his constitutional deputy, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, will assume presidential powers shortly before he goes into surgery.
Under the arrangement, announced last week after speculation about the Kremlin power structure, Chernomyrdin will sign a decree to hand authority back to Yeltsin after the operation.

Asked in an interview on NTV television how long it would be after surgery before Yeltsin had his finger back on the nuclear "button", the head of the presidential medical centre, Sergei Mironov, said: "I think after 24 hours. After he has completely come round from the anaesthetic."

Mironov, confirming details of the operation given on Wednesday, said Yeltsin would probably be readied for the operation only on the day before. The surgery itself would last an hour and a half to an hour and three quarters, he said.
Until the operation the president would stay at the elite Central Clinical Hospital or possibly spend some time at the Barvikha sanitorium just outside the capital.

It would take six to 10 weeks for him to be back to full working capacity, Mironov said. But he added that the president continued to work for two to three hours every day in a room in his hospital suite which doubles as his dining room.

Mironov said doctors may not decide until a few days before the operation whether to carry it out at the Central Clinical Hospital or at Moscow's Cardiological Centre, where the lead surgeon, Renat Akchurin, is based.
Mironov said the hospital had the facilities needed but that Akchurin might prefer to work in familiar surroundings.

"We're ready to do this operation either in the Cardiological Centre or in the Central Clinical Hospital," he said. "The issue of where the operation will be carried out will be decided in the last few days before the operation."
Sketching in a few details of Yeltsin's life in hospital, Mironov said the president's two daughters were visiting him every day while his wife, Naina, was by his side giving support.
Naina, 64, is convalescing at the same hospital after a kidney operation a month ago. Mironov said she was not in the same room, but "right nearby". She was "doing fine" herself.

She is not doing the cooking, however. During the spring election campaign Naina revealed that the president's favourite recipe was a heart-stopping chocolate-cake concoction she called "Black Man's Kiss". Now Yeltsin's food is being prepared by a dietician working under doctors' orders.
"Boris Nikolayevich is very unfussy," Mironov said. "They cook fairly tastily. I sometimes even have a taste myself."
"I wouldn't say the conditions are too sumptious, but in any case he has a fairly good bedroom with of course the whole suite, toilet, bathroom and so on," the doctor added.
Yeltsin was a hard man to keep inactive, he said, noting that his exertions in winning July's election had meant postponing treatment after two heart attacks last year.

"Boris Nikolayevich is a man with unbelievable human reserves, there are times when even we doctors are surprised and cannot understand his reserves of energy, of spiritual, physical and moral forces," Mironov said of his boss.
